sections.title: Selecting and filtering
sections.intro: Column lists, aliases, WHERE with comparison, BETWEEN, IN lists and LIKE, ORDER BY with LIMIT and OFFSET.

examples.label: Filters
examples.sql:
SELECT count(*) AS parts
FROM part
WHERE p_size BETWEEN 10 AND 12
  AND p_brand IN ('Brand#11', 'Brand#12')
  AND p_type NOT LIKE '%BRASS'

examples.label: Top N with an offset
examples.sql:
SELECT o_orderkey, o_totalprice
FROM orders
ORDER BY o_totalprice DESC
LIMIT 3 OFFSET 2

sections.title: Joins
sections.intro: INNER, LEFT and CROSS joins with ON, and comma joins with the condition in WHERE. The optimizer turns equality conditions into hash join keys and picks the order.

examples.label: Explicit join
examples.sql:
SELECT n_name, r_name
FROM nation
JOIN region ON n_regionkey = r_regionkey
ORDER BY n_name
LIMIT 3
examples.output:
n_name    | r_name
----------+--------
ALGERIA   | AFRICA
ARGENTINA | AMERICA
BRAZIL    | AMERICA
(3 rows)

examples.label: Left join that keeps unmatched rows
examples.sql:
SELECT c_mktsegment, count(o_orderkey) AS orders
FROM customer
LEFT JOIN orders ON o_custkey = c_custkey AND o_orderpriority = '1-URGENT'
GROUP BY c_mktsegment
ORDER BY c_mktsegment
examples.output:
c_mktsegment | orders
-------------+-------
AUTOMOBILE   | 609
BUILDING     | 704
FURNITURE    | 594
HOUSEHOLD    | 602
MACHINERY    | 511
(5 rows)

sections.title: Grouping and aggregates
sections.intro: count(*), count(x), count(DISTINCT x), sum, avg, min and max, with GROUP BY and HAVING. Grouping by an output position or alias works.

examples.label: HAVING and count(DISTINCT)
examples.sql:
SELECT p_brand, count(*) AS parts, count(DISTINCT p_size) AS sizes
FROM part
GROUP BY p_brand
HAVING count(*) > 70
ORDER BY p_brand
LIMIT 3

examples.label: Group by a CASE expression
examples.sql:
SELECT CASE WHEN o_totalprice > 300000 THEN 'big'
            WHEN o_totalprice > 100000 THEN 'mid'
            ELSE 'small' END AS size,
       count(*) AS orders
FROM orders
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 2 DESC
examples.output:
size  | orders
------+-------
mid   | 9149
small | 5319
big   | 532
(3 rows)

sections.title: Subqueries and CTEs
sections.intro: EXISTS, NOT EXISTS, IN and NOT IN subqueries, scalar subqueries (correlated or not), derived tables and WITH. The binder rewrites correlated subqueries into joins.

examples.label: Correlated EXISTS
examples.sql:
SELECT n_name
FROM nation n
WHERE EXISTS (
  SELECT 1 FROM supplier s
  WHERE s.s_nationkey = n.n_nationkey AND s_acctbal > 9900
)
ORDER BY n_name

examples.label: Correlated scalar subquery
examples.sql:
SELECT c_name,
       (SELECT count(*) FROM orders WHERE o_custkey = c_custkey) AS orders
FROM customer
ORDER BY orders DESC, c_name
LIMIT 3

examples.label: WITH
examples.sql:
WITH per_customer AS (
  SELECT o_custkey, count(*) AS n FROM orders GROUP BY o_custkey
)
SELECT max(n) AS most_orders, round(avg(n), 2) AS average
FROM per_customer

sections.title: Set operations
sections.intro: UNION, UNION ALL, EXCEPT and INTERSECT, with ORDER BY and LIMIT on the result.

examples.label: UNION ALL
examples.sql:
SELECT r_name AS name FROM region
UNION ALL
SELECT 'ATLANTIS'
ORDER BY name
LIMIT 3

examples.label: EXCEPT
examples.sql:
SELECT n_regionkey FROM nation
EXCEPT
SELECT r_regionkey FROM region WHERE r_name = 'ASIA'
ORDER BY 1

sections.title: Arithmetic and NULL
sections.intro: Integer division returns a double and division by zero returns infinity, as in DuckDB. NULL propagates through arithmetic; IS [NOT] DISTINCT FROM compares NULL safely.

examples.label: Division
examples.sql: SELECT 7 / 2 AS half, 7 % 3 AS remainder, 1 / 0 AS by_zero

examples.label: NULL handling
examples.sql:
SELECT 1 + NULL AS plus_null,
       coalesce(NULL, 2) AS first_value,
       nullif(3, 3) AS null_if_equal,
       NULL IS NOT DISTINCT FROM NULL AS same
examples.output:
plus_null | first_value | null_if_equal | same
----------+-------------+---------------+-----
NULL      | 2           | NULL          | true
(1 row)

examples.label: Casts
examples.sql:
SELECT CAST(3.7 AS INTEGER) AS i,
       CAST(42 AS VARCHAR) || '!' AS s,
       CAST('12' AS DOUBLE) AS d

sections.title: Dates
sections.intro: DATE literals, INTERVAL arithmetic in days, months and years, date differences in days, EXTRACT and the matching functions.

examples.label: Interval arithmetic
examples.sql:
SELECT DATE '1998-12-01' - INTERVAL '90' DAY AS cutoff,
       DATE '2024-02-29' + INTERVAL 1 YEAR AS next_year,
       DATE '1995-03-01' - DATE '1995-01-01' AS days

examples.label: Parts of a date
examples.sql:
SELECT EXTRACT(YEAR FROM DATE '1995-06-17') AS y,
       month(DATE '1995-06-17') AS m,
       quarter(DATE '1995-06-17') AS q,
       dayofweek(DATE '1995-06-17') AS dow

sections.title: Strings and numbers
sections.intro: String functions: || and concat, length, substring, upper, lower, trim, ltrim, rtrim, replace, reverse, starts_with, ends_with, contains, strpos. Numeric: abs, round, ceil, floor, sign, sqrt, power, ln, log10, exp, greatest, least.

examples.label: Strings
examples.sql:
SELECT 'quack' || 'less' AS joined,
       substring('quackless', 1, 5) AS sub,
       upper(trim('  duck ')) AS cleaned,
       replace('a-b-c', '-', '+') AS replaced,
       starts_with('duckdb', 'duck') AS prefix
examples.output:
joined    | sub   | cleaned | replaced | prefix
----------+-------+---------+----------+-------
quackless | quack | DUCK    | a+b+c    | true
(1 row)

examples.label: Numbers
examples.sql:
SELECT round(3.14159, 2) AS r,
       power(2, 10) AS p,
       sqrt(2.0) AS root,
       greatest(1, 5, 3) AS g,
       floor(-1.2) AS f
